title: 01.AI's Kai-Fu Lee on Pacing Frontier AI Development
summary: Kai-Fu Lee, CEO of 01.AI, says he suspects American AI companies may already have developed models that are "really great, but also really scary." He discusses this on "Bloomberg: The China Show" on the sidelines of the BNP Paribas Global Markets APAC Conference. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Schwab Is Neutral on Equities, Favorable on Commodities, Sonders Says
summary: Liz Ann Sonders, Charles Schwab chief investment strategist, says there is no one asset allocation that makes sense for every investor. She says the firm is neutral on equities, less favorable on fixed income, and more favorable on commodities.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: BNY Chief Economist on Fed Rate Hike, BOJ Outlook

title: DoubleLine’s Gundlach Warns of Fiscal Crisis in Next Recession
summary: DoubleLine Capital chief executive Jeffrey Gundlach warned that the next US downturn could trigger a debt crisis that sends long-term Treasury yields sharply higher — defying decades of conventional wisdom that bonds will always serve as safe haven during times of economic strife.

title: US to Sell F-35s to Saudi Arabia in $24.3 Billion Deal
summary:
The State Department notified Congress that it plans to sell Saudi Arabia up to 48 F-35 warplanes in a first-time sale that could be worth as much as $24.3 billion. The sale of the Lockheed Martin Corp. fighter jet to Saudi Arabia has been in the works for a number of years. President Donald Trump signaled in November the US would sell F-35s to the Kingdom, offering Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman a prize he’s long cherished, ahead of a visit to the White House that month. Meantime, the Pentagon and Lockheed Martin Corp. are moving to speed up the production of a new classified air-to-air missile for US Air Force and Navy jets that’s seen as vital to deterring China.

For more, we speak with Wayne Sanders, Senior Defense Research Analyst for Bloomberg Intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Jeni’s Splendid Ice Creams Founder on New Fiber Company
summary: Jeni Britton, founder of Jeni’s Splendid Ice Creams and now Founder and CEO of Floura, discussed her shift from ice cream to fiber-based snacks made from produce trim like apple cores, watermelon rinds, mango and pineapple rinds. Britton highlighted Starbucks as an important validation point for the young company, saying the placement gives Floura higher visibility and credibility as it expands beyond its direct-to-consumer roots. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Carry Trade Explained: Why the Japanese Yen Is Losing Its Appeal (JPY/USD)
summary: For decades, the Japanese yen has been one of the world’s favored currencies for investors looking to borrow cheaply and put that money into assets offering higher returns.

title: Saudi Pivots Oil Routes After Pipeline Attack
summary: Saudi Arabia is ramping up prompt sales of crude from outside the Strait of Hormuz following the shutdown of the kingdom’s East-West pipeline, which halted cross-country flows to its Red Sea coast. The sale helped attribute to a fall in oil prices as physical markets cooled from recent peaks as traders bet some Middle East supply outages would be short-lived. Noam Raydan, William Sudhaus Senior Fellow at the Washington Institute, joins Bloomberg Businessweek to discuss why the Saudi pipeline is so crucial and what the attack on the pipeline could mean for the broader Saudi oil industry. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Japan’s Retail Bond Boom Offers New Avenue for Fiscal Funding
summary: Japan’s rising yields are drawing record demand for retail government bonds, offering a potential new source of funding just as policymakers seek to contain borrowing costs and reduce market supply.

title: Gold Surges Along With US Treasuries as Oil Price Slide Deepens
summary: Gold rallied alongside Treasuries as a slump in oil prices helped ease concerns about inflation, following the Federal Reserve’s first interest-rate hike since 2023.

title: Stocks, Bonds Rise After Fed-Day Drop as Oil Falls: Markets Wrap

title: Oil Drops as Traders See Supply Outages Proving Short-Lived

title: Suspended Glencore Executive Told Radiant ‘Say Nothing on Email’

title: Small Town America Confronts Data Centers, Rejects Some Plans
summary:
Bloomberg's Shruti Singh joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Real Yield." Blackstone-owned QTS proposed a massive data center in Clinton, Iowa, that would bring thousands of construction jobs and provide nearly $200 million in property taxes in its first 10 years. Many residents though want nothing to do with the data center and view it as a potential source of noise pollution, environmental degradation and rising utility costs - rejecting what some fear will do more harm than good, even if that means sacrificing economic growth.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Braskem Creditors Shun Debt Plan, Push Owners to Inject Cash

Bloomberg's Aashna Shah joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Real Yield." US state and local government bonds are near their cheapest levels relative to Treasuries in a year as heavy issuance and fading demand collide with a broader fixed-income selloff.
